source: OpenStax A&P 2e: 8.2 Bones of the Upper Limb (and glossary); 8.5; 9.4

main.t: A small wrist bone at the base of the index finger, second in the second row of carpal bones (trapezoid).

simpler.t: The trapezoid is a small wrist bone at the base of your index finger.

deeper.t: It meets only one metacarpal, the second, which is firmly anchored and does not move.

facts.t: It is the second bone of the distal row, counting from the thumb side.
The trapezium is beside it on the thumb side, and the capitate on the other side.
The scaphoid is above it, and the second metacarpal below.

simpler.t: It sits between the base of the thumb and the middle of the wrist.

deeper.t: Ligaments hold it together with the other bones of its row.

items.name: Surface for the second metacarpal
items.t: Its lower surface, at the carpometacarpal joint.

items.name: Side surfaces
items.t: It meets the trapezium on one side and the capitate on the other.

simpler.t: It is a small block of bone with joints on four sides.

deeper.t: Its joints with its neighbours are plane (gliding) joints, which allow small sliding movements.

facts.t: It supports the second metacarpal, which is firmly anchored and does not move.
Its plane joints with the neighbouring carpal bones allow only small sliding movements.
With the other carpal bones it forms the walls and floor of the carpal tunnel.

simpler.t: It gives the index finger’s palm bone a firm base.

items.name: Second metacarpal
items.t: Meets its lower surface at the carpometacarpal joint.

items.name: Scaphoid
items.t: Meets it above, at the midcarpal joint.

items.name: Trapezium
items.t: Its neighbour on the thumb side.

items.name: Capitate
items.t: Its neighbour on the little-finger side.

items.name: Intercarpal joints
items.t: Plane joints between neighbouring carpal bones.

simpler.t: It is wedged between the trapezium, the capitate, the scaphoid and the second metacarpal.

facts.t: It forms by replacing a cartilage model with bone (endochondral ossification), like all limb bones except the clavicle.
Its single ossification centre appears at about the eighth year.
facts.check: Not in OpenStax A&P 2e (chapters 6–9, 12–16, 20). Gray’s 1918 (8.2) gives the eighth year (as the “lesser multangular”) (supporting only).

items.injury: Overuse of the tendons or a wrist injury makes the contents of the carpal tunnel swell.
items.damaged: The nerve in the tunnel, whose walls and floor the carpal bones form.
items.cannotDo: Use the hand without pain, numbness or weakness (carpal tunnel syndrome).
items.why: The bony walls and floor and the tough roof cannot stretch, so swelling presses on the nerve.

items.injury: A hard bony lump on the back of the hand, at the base of the index and middle fingers.
items.damaged: Extra bone (a carpal boss) where the trapezoid and capitate meet the second and third metacarpals.
items.cannotDo: Bend the wrist back fully without pain over the lump.
items.why: The lump catches the tendons that run over the back of the wrist.

items.q: Explain why the second metacarpal hardly moves.
model: The second and third metacarpals are firmly anchored in place.
The second metacarpal meets the trapezoid (and the trapezium).
The distal carpal bones are held together by ligaments.
The fourth and fifth metacarpals, by contrast, move a little.

items.q: Compare the joints of the trapezoid with those of the trapezium.
model: The trapezoid has plane joints with its neighbours, allowing small sliding movements.
It meets only the second metacarpal, which is immobile.
The trapezium forms a saddle joint with the first metacarpal.
So the thumb moves widely while the base of the index finger stays fixed.

items.q: Using the order of the carpal bones, predict where the trapezoid lies.
model: The second row runs from the thumb side: trapezium, trapezoid, capitate, hamate.
So the trapezoid is second from the thumb side.
It lies between the trapezium and the capitate.
The scaphoid is above it and the second metacarpal below.

check.stem: Which metacarpal does the trapezoid meet?
check.why: It meets only the second metacarpal.

check.stem: What type of joints join the trapezoid to its neighbouring carpal bones?
Which bone lies directly above (proximal to) the trapezoid?
